newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex says may allow U.S. West Coast trial runs.
newsitem.headline: Pemex says may allow U.S. West Coast trial runs.

text.p: Mexico is working on mechanisms to allow trial shipments of crude to U.S. West Coast refineries, even if the buyers are not established customers of state oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos, a top Pemex trader told Reuters on Tuesday.
Mexican law obliges Pemex to sell crude only to refineries and end users with at least a one-year contract.
But in a bid to revive exports to the West Coast, the trader said Pemex is working to allow some initial trial runs for potential clients that do not have a contract with Pemex.
"The test runs would not oblige them to a contract, but they would have to respect the conditions under which we operate," said the trader, who asked not to be identified.
He said Pemex had not yet decided to allow the trial shipments.
Mexico last sold crude to the West Coast in 1991, and is hoping to revive sales there in an effort to boost exports.
Negotiations with West Coast buyers are "going well," but nothing has been firmed up yet, the trader added.
West Coast refineries have said they are interested in using Mexico's heavy Maya crude. One trader spoke of a trial shipment possibly in July.

The trader said Pemex is eyeing refinery clients in San Francisco and Washington state as an alternative to Los Angeles, which has stricter emissions legislation. The laws could prohibit the processing of Maya, which has a high sulfur content of API 22.
